insights.insight: The protocol has cryptographically verified $1.1M in real transactions across 17,969 receipts — not modeled intent, not inferred behavior, but confirmed purchases tied to specific brands and categories. For marketers paying $5+ CPM for probabilistic targeting, this is the same signal without the inference layer.

insights.topic: Category breadth now covers digital and AI-native commerce
insights.insight: A single overnight update on May 2 doubled the verified vendor list to 20, adding Amazon, Stripe, Anthropic, OpenAI, and others — meaning verifiable purchase signals now extend beyond physical retail into SaaS, subscriptions, and AI services. Brands competing in digital categories have a new attribution surface.

insights.topic: Grocery and restaurant categories dominate verified spend
insights.insight: In the trailing 14 days, grocery-supermarkets (985 receipts, $41K) and restaurants-dining (952 receipts, $35K) lead all categories, with Walmart, Costco, and Target as the top verified brands. For CPG and QSR marketers specifically, the existing receipt corpus already maps their competitive battleground.

insights.topic: Geographic diffusion is real but episodic
insights.insight: The May 2 heartbeat recorded a 23-CBSA single-pulse burst at 100% diffusion — the largest in observation history — but typical readings hold 19 active metros, suggesting geographic reach is broad but not yet structurally consistent across all markets.

7-day GMV has contracted 63% from its April 13 peak of $211K to a $66K–$86K weekly band, with acceleration holding just below 1.0x for five consecutive readings. The floor pattern indicates a stable but slower-growing data supply — sufficient for panel-scale insights, not yet at media-network scale.

insights.topic: Regional and independent retail entering the signal set
insights.insight: J&H Family Stores appeared in the 14-day brand list on May 2 alongside national chains, indicating organic user adoption is pulling in regional convenience and grocery operators that are invisible in most first-party data programs. For brands trying to measure performance outside major retail, this is a structurally undervalued signal.
